paragraphs.title: The Command to Go Up to Bethel and Purify Themselves

easy.question: Where did God command Jacob to go?
easy.explanation: God commanded Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel.”

easy.question: What did Jacob command his household to remove?
easy.explanation: Jacob told them to put away the foreign gods that were among them.

easy.question: What did Jacob and his household do with the objects they had?
answers: They buried them under the oak
easy.explanation: They gave Jacob the foreign gods and earrings, and he hid them under the oak.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in these verses?
answers: God commands Jacob to go to Bethel, and Jacob speaks to his household
The household buries the objects, and then God commands Jacob
Jacob builds an altar, and then the household removes the foreign gods
medium.explanation: First God commands Jacob, then Jacob commands his household, and finally they give him the objects.

medium.question: Why did Jacob want to build an altar at Bethel?
answers: To thank God for answering him and being with him in his distress and journey
medium.explanation: Jacob remembers that God answered him in his distress and was with him on his journey, so he wants to build an altar.

medium.question: In the phrase “Put away the strange gods ... and be clean,” what does “be clean” mean?
medium.explanation: Removing the foreign gods and changing clothes shows that they were to prepare and purify themselves for worship.

challenge.question: What is the connection between Jacob’s flight from Esau and the command to build an altar at Bethel?
answers: Jacob remembers God’s past protection and wants to thank him
Jacob wants to fight Esau again
Jacob is told to build an altar where Esau lived
challenge.explanation: The verse recalls God’s appearing to Jacob when he fled, showing that the altar expresses gratitude for God’s protection.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that everyone in the household gave up the foreign gods and earrings?
answers: They hid their possessions from Jacob
They accepted Jacob’s command and abandoned objects connected with idolatry
They were preparing to trade at Bethel
challenge.explanation: Giving the objects to Jacob and then burying them shows that they acted together to turn away from foreign worship.

challenge.question: What important detail does the verse give about where the objects were buried?
answers: They were buried in the wilderness
They were buried under the oak near Shechem
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the objects were buried under the oak by Shechem, not at Bethel, where they were going.

questions.question: What is the connection between Jacob’s flight from Esau and the command to build an altar at Bethel?
answers: Jacob remembers God’s past protection and wants to thank him
Jacob wants to fight Esau again
Jacob is told to build an altar where Esau lived
questions.explanation: The verse recalls God’s appearing to Jacob when he fled, showing that the altar expresses gratitude for God’s protection.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that everyone in the household gave up the foreign gods and earrings?
answers: They hid their possessions from Jacob
They accepted Jacob’s command and abandoned objects connected with idolatry
They were preparing to trade at Bethel
questions.explanation: Giving the objects to Jacob and then burying them shows that they acted together to turn away from foreign worship.

questions.question: What important detail does the verse give about where the objects were buried?
answers: They were buried in the wilderness
They were buried under the oak near Shechem
questions.explanation: The verse says that the objects were buried under the oak by Shechem, not at Bethel, where they were going.

paragraphs.title: The Journey to Bethel and the Building of the Altar

easy.question: Who arrived at Luz, which is also called Bethel?
answers: Jacob and all the people with him
The kings of the surrounding cities
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that Jacob came to Luz, which is Bethel, together with all the people who were with him.

easy.question: What did Jacob build at Bethel?
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “And he built there an altar.”

easy.question: Who died and was buried under the oak?
easy.explanation: Verse 8 tells of the death and burial of Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse.

medium.question: Why did the people in the surrounding cities not pursue Jacob’s sons?
answers: Because the terror of God was upon them
Because Jacob asked them for peace
medium.explanation: The verse connects God’s terror upon the cities with their not pursuing Jacob’s sons.

medium.question: What does the verse say about the relationship between Luz and Bethel?
answers: Bethel was outside the land of Canaan
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Luz in the land of Canaan was Bethel.

medium.question: In the phrase “the terror of God was upon the cities,” what does “terror” mean?
medium.explanation: The context shows that the people were afraid, since they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.

challenge.question: Why did Jacob call the place “El-bethel”?
answers: Because the kings of Canaan lived there
Because God had appeared to him there before
challenge.explanation: Jacob gave it this name because God had appeared to him there when he fled from his brother.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Jacob arrived at Bethel with all the people who were with him?
answers: The entire group traveling with him made the journey
He sent his family somewhere else
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Jacob arrived with all the people who were with him, so the whole group made the journey.

challenge.question: Why was the oak called “Allon-bachuth”?
answers: Because a joyful celebration took place beneath it
Because Deborah was buried beneath it and people mourned her death
Because it was a small, dry tree
challenge.explanation: The name is connected with Deborah’s death and burial, which brought mourning and weeping.

questions.question: Why did Jacob call the place “El-bethel”?
answers: Because the kings of Canaan lived there
Because God had appeared to him there before
questions.explanation: Jacob gave it this name because God had appeared to him there when he fled from his brother.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Jacob arrived at Bethel with all the people who were with him?
answers: The entire group traveling with him made the journey
He sent his family somewhere else
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Jacob arrived with all the people who were with him, so the whole group made the journey.

questions.question: Why was the oak called “Allon-bachuth”?
answers: Because a joyful celebration took place beneath it
Because Deborah was buried beneath it and people mourned her death
Because it was a small, dry tree
questions.explanation: The name is connected with Deborah’s death and burial, which brought mourning and weeping.

paragraphs.title: The Blessing, the Change of Name, and the Promise of the Land

easy.question: To whom did God appear in this chapter?
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that God appeared to Jacob.

easy.question: What new name did God give Jacob?
easy.explanation: God told Jacob, “Your name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be your name.”

easy.question: What did Jacob set up where God spoke to him?
easy.explanation: Jacob set up a pillar there, a stone memorial.

medium.question: What did God do after promising Jacob a people and a land?
answers: He went with Jacob to Egypt
He built an altar for him
medium.explanation: After the promises, the text says, “And God went up from him.”

medium.question: In the phrase “a pillar of stone,” what is a pillar?
answers: A stone or post set up as a memorial
medium.explanation: A stone pillar was set up at the place as a sign and memorial.

medium.question: What two central promises did Jacob receive?
medium.explanation: God promised that Jacob would multiply and receive the land given to Abraham and Isaac.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the word “again” in “God appeared unto Jacob again”?
answers: God had appeared to Jacob before
This was the first time God appeared to Jacob
challenge.explanation: The word “again” indicates that this was an additional appearance after earlier ones.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “kings shall come out of thy loins” mean?
answers: Kings would come from Jacob’s sons and descendants
Kings would come to visit Jacob
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to descendants, meaning that kings would come from Jacob’s offspring.

challenge.question: Why did Jacob call the place “Bethel”?
answers: Because his first son was born there
Because he found a special stone there
Because God spoke to him there
challenge.explanation: Verse 15 says that Jacob called the place Bethel because God spoke to him there.

questions.question: What can we understand from the word “again” in “God appeared unto Jacob again”?
answers: God had appeared to Jacob before
This was the first time God appeared to Jacob
questions.explanation: The word “again” indicates that this was an additional appearance after earlier ones.

questions.question: What does the phrase “kings shall come out of thy loins” mean?
answers: Kings would come from Jacob’s sons and descendants
Kings would come to visit Jacob
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to descendants, meaning that kings would come from Jacob’s offspring.

questions.question: Why did Jacob call the place “Bethel”?
answers: Because his first son was born there
Because he found a special stone there
Because God spoke to him there
questions.explanation: Verse 15 says that Jacob called the place Bethel because God spoke to him there.

easy.question: From where did Jacob and his family travel?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And they journeyed from Bethel.”

easy.question: Who said to Rachel, “Fear not”?
easy.explanation: The midwife told Rachel not to be afraid because she would have a son.

easy.question: What name did Jacob give Rachel’s son?
easy.explanation: Rachel called him Benoni, but his father Jacob called him Benjamin.

medium.question: Why did the midwife say to Rachel, “Fear not”?
answers: Because she would also have a son
Because the family had reached Bethel
Because Jacob had already named the child
medium.explanation: The midwife comforted Rachel by telling her that the birth would result in a son.

medium.question: In the phrase “there was but a little way to come to Ephrath,” what does “a little way” describe?
medium.explanation: The phrase “a little way to come to Ephrath” refers to the short distance still remaining before they reached Ephrath.

medium.question: What did Jacob do after Rachel was buried?
answers: He gave her a new name
He set up a pillar over her grave
medium.explanation: The verse says that Jacob set up a pillar over Rachel’s grave.

challenge.question: What can be learned from Rachel calling the child “Benoni” and Jacob calling him “Benjamin”?
answers: The mother and father gave the child different names
Rachel and Jacob agreed on the same name
The child gave himself two names
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Rachel gave him one name and his father Jacob gave him another.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “unto this day” emphasize?
answers: The pillar remained or was remembered when the account was written
Jacob set up the pillar before Benjamin was born
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the pillar remained or was still known at a later time.

challenge.question: What geographical identification appears in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse explains that Ephrath is Bethlehem: “in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.”

questions.question: What can be learned from Rachel calling the child “Benoni” and Jacob calling him “Benjamin”?
answers: The mother and father gave the child different names
Rachel and Jacob agreed on the same name
The child gave himself two names
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Rachel gave him one name and his father Jacob gave him another.

questions.question: What does the phrase “unto this day” emphasize?
answers: The pillar remained or was remembered when the account was written
Jacob set up the pillar before Benjamin was born
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the pillar remained or was still known at a later time.

questions.question: What geographical identification appears in the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse explains that Ephrath is Bethlehem: “in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem.”

paragraphs.title: The Move to the Tower of Edar and the Growing Family

easy.question: Where did Israel travel and pitch his tent?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel journeyed and spread his tent beyond the tower of Edar.

easy.question: Who lay with Bilhah?
easy.explanation: The verse says explicitly, “Reuben went and lay with Bilhah.”

easy.question: How many sons did Jacob have?
easy.explanation: At the end of the passage it says, “Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.”

medium.question: What can be understood from the statement that Reuben acted “when Israel dwelt in that land”?
answers: The act happened after Israel had settled there
The act happened before Israel began his journey
The act happened while Israel was in Egypt
medium.explanation: The statement indicates that Israel was already living and settled in the land at that time.

medium.question: In the phrase “Bilhah his father’s concubine,” what is a concubine?
answers: A woman with a secondary marital status
A servant who worked in the house
medium.explanation: Here, “concubine” describes a partner of the father who was not his principal wife.

medium.question: What order of events is described in the verses?
answers: Reuben lay with Bilhah, Israel traveled, and then Jacob’s sons were born
Jacob’s sons were born, then Israel traveled, and then Reuben acted
Israel traveled and settled, Reuben lay with Bilhah, and Israel heard about it
medium.explanation: First Israel traveled and pitched his tent, then Reuben acted, and finally the text says that Israel heard about it.

challenge.question: What does the verse say about Israel’s response after hearing what Reuben had done?
answers: It gives no response, only saying that he heard
challenge.explanation: The verse only says, “And Israel heard it,” without describing his response.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the use of the names “Israel” and “Jacob” in this passage?
answers: Both names refer to the same father, Jacob
Israel was one of Jacob’s sons
challenge.explanation: Israel was Jacob’s other name, so both names refer to the same person.

challenge.question: What important detail appears immediately after the account of Reuben’s act and Israel’s hearing about it?
answers: Israel returned to the tower of Edar
challenge.explanation: The verse ends by stating that Jacob’s sons were twelve.

questions.question: What does the verse say about Israel’s response after hearing what Reuben had done?
answers: It gives no response, only saying that he heard
questions.explanation: The verse only says, “And Israel heard it,” without describing his response.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the use of the names “Israel” and “Jacob” in this passage?
answers: Both names refer to the same father, Jacob
Israel was one of Jacob’s sons
questions.explanation: Israel was Jacob’s other name, so both names refer to the same person.

questions.question: What important detail appears immediately after the account of Reuben’s act and Israel’s hearing about it?
answers: Israel returned to the tower of Edar
questions.explanation: The verse ends by stating that Jacob’s sons were twelve.

easy.question: Who were the sons of Leah mentioned in these verses?
answers: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun
easy.explanation: The verse lists Leah’s six sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

easy.question: Who were Rachel’s sons?
easy.explanation: Verse 24 says, “The sons of Rachel; Joseph, and Benjamin.”

easy.question: Who were Bilhah’s sons?
easy.explanation: Verse 25 says that Bilhah’s sons were Dan and Naphtali.

medium.question: Which woman is credited with the most sons in these verses?
medium.explanation: Leah is credited with six sons, while Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah each have two.

medium.question: What does “Rachel’s handmaid” mean in this passage?
medium.explanation: A handmaid was a female servant; the passage identifies Bilhah as Rachel’s handmaid.

medium.question: Which group is mentioned immediately after Rachel’s sons?
medium.explanation: After Rachel’s sons, verse 25 mentions Bilhah’s sons, Dan and Naphtali.

challenge.question: What is the total number of Jacob’s sons mentioned in these verses?
challenge.explanation: Leah had six sons, and Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah had two each, making twelve altogether.

challenge.question: What do Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher have in common?
answers: They were all sons of handmaids
challenge.explanation: Dan and Naphtali were sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid, and Gad and Asher were sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid.

challenge.question: What detail does the final verse emphasize about Jacob’s sons?
answers: They were all born in Egypt
They were born to Jacob in Padanaram
challenge.explanation: The final verse says, “These are the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Padanaram.”

questions.question: What is the total number of Jacob’s sons mentioned in these verses?
questions.explanation: Leah had six sons, and Rachel, Bilhah, and Zilpah had two each, making twelve altogether.

questions.question: What do Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher have in common?
answers: They were all sons of handmaids
questions.explanation: Dan and Naphtali were sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid, and Gad and Asher were sons of Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid.

questions.question: What detail does the final verse emphasize about Jacob’s sons?
answers: They were all born in Egypt
They were born to Jacob in Padanaram
questions.explanation: The final verse says, “These are the sons of Jacob, which were born to him in Padanaram.”

paragraphs.title: Jacob Comes to Isaac and Isaac’s Death

easy.question: Who came to Isaac his father?
easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “And Jacob came unto Isaac his father.”

easy.question: How old was Isaac when he died?
easy.explanation: Verse 28 says that Isaac lived one hundred eighty years.

easy.question: Who buried Isaac?
easy.explanation: The end of verse 29 says that Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.

medium.question: At what place did Jacob come to Isaac?
medium.explanation: The verse identifies Mamre, the city of Arbah, as Hebron.

medium.question: In the phrase “where Abraham and Isaac sojourned,” what does “sojourned” mean?
medium.explanation: To sojourn means to live or stay in a place, and the verse says this was where Abraham and Isaac lived.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Isaac was buried, and then Jacob came to him
Isaac died, and then Jacob was born
Jacob came to Isaac, Isaac died, and his two sons buried him
medium.explanation: First Jacob came to Isaac, then Isaac died, and finally Esau and Jacob buried him.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “Mamre, the city of Arbah, which is Hebron” teach us?
answers: These are different names for the same place
challenge.explanation: The wording identifies Mamre, Arbah, and Hebron as names associated with the same place.

challenge.question: What does “old and full of days” mean in the description of Isaac?
answers: Isaac was old and had lived a full life
Isaac had suffered from hunger for years
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes someone who had reached old age and lived through many full years.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Esau and Jacob burying Isaac together?
answers: Only Esau remained in contact with Isaac
Jacob did not take part in his father’s burial
Both sons took part in honoring their father at his burial
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly names Esau and Jacob as those who buried Isaac, so both took part in his burial.

answers: These are different names for the same place
questions.explanation: The wording identifies Mamre, Arbah, and Hebron as names associated with the same place.

answers: Isaac was old and had lived a full life
Isaac had suffered from hunger for years
questions.explanation: The phrase describes someone who had reached old age and lived through many full years.

answers: Only Esau remained in contact with Isaac

questions.explanation: The verse explicitly names Esau and Jacob as those who buried Isaac, so both took part in his burial.
